title: Presentations and Discussion
tagline: Planning a talk, signposting, delivery, visual aids, handling questions, seminars and group discussion, debate and persuasion, meetings and negotiation, and interviews
summary: Speaking at length and in groups needs structure, clear delivery and the language to manage interaction. This course covers planning and signposting a presentation, using the voice and visual aids, handling questions, taking part in seminars and discussions, debating and persuading, meetings and negotiations, and job and academic interviews.

chapters.title: Planning a talk
chapters.summary: Audience, purpose and a clear structure with an opening, main points and an ending.

chapters.title: Signposting a talk
chapters.summary: The phrases that guide listeners through a talk: introducing, moving on, summarising and concluding.

chapters.title: Delivery
chapters.summary: Pace, pausing, stress and intonation, eye contact, and managing nerves.

chapters.title: Visual aids
chapters.summary: Designing simple slides, and describing charts and images in a talk.

chapters.title: Handling questions
chapters.summary: Inviting, clarifying and answering questions, and what to say when you do not know the answer.

chapters.title: Seminars and group discussion
chapters.summary: Taking the floor, building on other people’s points, disagreeing constructively and bringing others in.

chapters.title: Debate and persuasion
chapters.summary: The structure of a formal debate, persuasive arguments and rebuttals.

chapters.title: Meetings and negotiation
chapters.summary: Chairing and taking part in meetings, making proposals, bargaining and reaching agreement.

chapters.title: Interviews
chapters.summary: Preparing for and answering questions in job and academic interviews, and asking your own.
